verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's first-party docs describe targeting conditions on rules that are evaluated against attributes passed into the SDK. They also cover saved groups as reusable segments, and layering multiple rules to serve different values to different users. Consistent assignment across SDKs is documented as well. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of saved groups (only a single mention), independent or hands-on corroboration of attribute-based targeting (the runtime probe only evaluated a default value).

support.subject: As a developer, I can target flags with attribute-based rules and reusable segments so the right users see the right variation

citations.quote: Add targeting conditions to a rule to control which values a user sees. Conditions are evaluated against attributes you pass into the SDK
Target feature flags with user attributes, conditions, saved groups, and percentage rollouts.
Layer multiple rules on one feature to compose behavior — for example, a forced value for beta testers above a gradual rollout to everyone else.
All SDKs use the same assignment logic, so the same attributes always produce the same variation regardless of which SDK you use.
